title.value: Automate email unsubscribes, calendar events, and shopping in a browser

introduction.value: A hands-on test of Comet's browser agent handling unsubscribes, calendar events, shopping, LinkedIn posts, research and an Instacart lasagna cart, with mixed results on complex workflows.

method.value: The Reddit post summarizes a hands-on Comet browser demo where the agent was connected to live sites like Gmail, Google Calendar, shopping sites, LinkedIn, Instacart, Reddit, and research tabs. It handled click-and-fill tasks such as unsubscribing some promotional emails, creating four Taco Tuesday events, comparing Walmart and Target prices, building an Instacart lasagna cart, and drafting a LinkedIn post, with human confirmation required for sensitive actions and help needed when flows got tricky.

outcome.value: It worked well on structured browser chores and could run tasks across tabs, but stalled on harder unsubscribe flows, struggled with complex apps like Photopea, and hit login, region, or site-security friction. The post’s concrete wins include four calendar events created and old non-lasagna cart items removed before checkout.

notes.value: The main catch is privacy and reliability: the post recommends using a separate Comet profile and reviewing its default data-retention settings before giving it account access.

source_text.body:
Automate email unsubscribes, calendar events, and shopping in a browser
A hands-on test of Comet's browser agent handling unsubscribes, calendar events, shopping, LinkedIn posts, research and an Instacart lasagna cart, with mixed results on complex workflows.
Done with
PC
Perplexity Comet
What they did
The Reddit post summarizes a hands-on Comet browser demo where the agent was connected to live sites like Gmail, Google Calendar, shopping sites, LinkedIn, Instacart, Reddit, and research tabs. It handled click-and-fill tasks such as unsubscribing some promotional emails, creating four Taco Tuesday events, comparing Walmart and Target prices, building an Instacart lasagna cart, and drafting a LinkedIn post, with human confirmation required for sensitive actions and help needed when flows got tricky.
How it went
It worked well on structured browser chores and could run tasks across tabs, but stalled on harder unsubscribe flows, struggled with complex apps like Photopea, and hit login, region, or site-security friction. The post’s concrete wins include four calendar events created and old non-lasagna cart items removed before checkout.
Worth knowing
The main catch is privacy and reliability: the post recommends using a separate Comet profile and reviewing its default data-retention settings before giving it account access.
Try it yourself
with
Perplexity Comet
Copy prompt
In my browser, go through my recent promotional emails in [Gmail or other inbox], list the senders you propose to unsubscribe from, and wait for my okay. After I approve, unsubscribe from them and give me a summary of which ones worked and which failed. Do not unsubscribe, delete anything, or buy anything without showing me what you are about to do first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/AIGuild/comments/1mad90a/comet_browser_tested_voice_agents_that_click_shop
